famousPlaces.name: Shibuya Crossing
famousPlaces.description: The world's busiest pedestrian crossing, where up to 3,000 people cross simultaneously from all directions. Surrounded by neon billboards and towering screens, it's the pulsating heart of modern Tokyo — best experienced from the Starbucks or Mag's Park rooftop above.
tips: Visit at night for the full neon effect
Grab a window seat at the Starbucks above for the best aerial view
Weekends are significantly more crowded

famousPlaces.name: Senso-ji Temple
famousPlaces.description: Tokyo's oldest and most revered Buddhist temple, founded in 628 AD in the Asakusa district. The iconic Kaminarimon Thunder Gate with its giant red lantern leads to Nakamise shopping street, lined with traditional crafts and snacks before the main hall.
tips: Arrive before 8AM to experience the temple without crowds
Draw an omikuji (fortune paper) — if bad, tie it to the rack
The Nakamise Dori shopping street opens around 10AM

famousPlaces.name: Fushimi Inari Shrine
famousPlaces.description: A breathtaking tunnel of over 10,000 vibrant vermillion torii gates that winds up Mount Inari. Dedicated to Inari, the Shinto god of foxes, rice, and prosperity, this is Kyoto's most iconic sight — a two-hour hike takes you to the mountain summit with panoramic views.
tips: Go at sunrise or late afternoon to avoid tour groups
The higher you climb, the fewer people you'll encounter
Wear comfortable shoes — it's 4km round trip with elevation

famousPlaces.name: Eiffel Tower
famousPlaces.description: Gustave Eiffel's iron masterpiece is the world's most-visited monument, rising 330 meters above the Seine. Built in 1889 and initially condemned by Parisian critics, it's now the defining symbol of France. The summit view stretches 70km on a clear day, with Champagne available at the top.
famousPlaces.bestTimeToVisit: Dusk or after 9PM for light show
tips: Book summit tickets 2 months in advance
The hourly light show runs until 1AM and is free to watch from Trocadéro
Taking the stairs to the 2nd floor is cheaper and faster than the queue

famousPlaces.name: The Louvre Museum
famousPlaces.description: The world's largest art museum and home to over 380,000 works including the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and Winged Victory. The stunning glass pyramid entrance designed by I.M. Pei creates a magnificent contrast with the 800-year-old palace that surrounds it.
tips: Pre-book timed entry tickets to avoid the pyramid queue
Wednesday & Friday evenings are significantly less crowded
Download the Louvre app for interactive maps and artwork guides

famousPlaces.name: Burj Khalifa
famousPlaces.description: At 828 meters, the Burj Khalifa is the world's tallest building — a tapering silver spire that pierces the desert sky and can be seen from 95km away. The At the Top observation deck on floor 124 and the premium SKY level on floor 148 offer vertigo-inducing views across the Gulf and desert.
tips: Book the SKY level (floor 148) for a more exclusive experience with fewer crowds
Arrive 30 minutes before sunset to witness the transition from day to the illuminated city at night
The Dubai Fountain show below runs every 30 minutes after 6PM

famousPlaces.name: Palm Jumeirah
famousPlaces.description: The world's largest artificial island, shaped like a palm tree and visible from space, is home to ultra-luxury hotels including the Atlantis and the One&Only. The Palm Monorail connects its fronds, and the boardwalk offers stunning views of the Dubai Marina skyline.
famousPlaces.bestTimeToVisit: Late afternoon for golden hour photography
tips: Take the Palm Monorail for a unique overhead view of the island
Aquaventure Waterpark at Atlantis is a full day attraction
The Pointe mall area on the tip has great skyline views

famousPlaces.name: Marina Bay Sands
famousPlaces.description: One of the most recognizable buildings in Asia — three 55-story towers topped by a 340-meter-long SkyPark with the world's largest rooftop infinity pool. The complex includes the ArtScience Museum, a luxury casino, and a rooftop observation deck offering stunning panoramic views.
tips: Hotel guests have exclusive access to the infinity pool — worth considering for a splurge
The non-hotel observation deck offers similar views at a fraction of the cost
Spectra light show at Event Plaza is free every night at 8PM and 9PM

famousPlaces.name: Gardens by the Bay
famousPlaces.description: An otherworldly 101-hectare nature park featuring the Supertree Grove — 16-story vertical gardens that come alive with a spectacular light and sound show each evening. The Cloud Forest dome contains a 35-meter indoor waterfall and mountain shrouded in mist inside a climate-controlled greenhouse.
famousPlaces.bestTimeToVisit: Evening, for the Garden Rhapsody light show at 7:45PM
tips: Garden Rhapsody show is free and runs every evening at 7:45PM and 8:45PM
The OCBC Skyway walkway between Supertrees is worth the extra fee
Combine with Marina Bay Sands visit in the same evening

famousPlaces.name: Central Park
famousPlaces.description: The 843-acre green lung of Manhattan is the world's most-visited urban park — a masterpiece of landscape design with meadows, woodland, a lake, an ice-skating rink, and famous sights like Bethesda Fountain, Strawberry Fields, and Belvedere Castle. The skyline views from the park are unmatched.
tips: Rent a bicycle to cover more ground
The Loeb Boathouse restaurant is perfect for a leisurely lunch by the lake
Strawberry Fields memorial is a tranquil tribute to John Lennon

famousPlaces.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
famousPlaces.description: The Met is the largest art museum in the Americas, spanning 17 acres and containing over 1.5 million works from 5,000 years of human history. From Egyptian mummies to Impressionist masterpieces to medieval armor, a single visit barely scratches the surface. The rooftop garden offers Central Park panoramas.
famousPlaces.openingHours: 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM (Thu–Sat until 9:00 PM; closed Tuesday)
tips: Thursday evenings are the least crowded time to visit
The Temple of Dendur and the Egyptian collection are must-sees
The rooftop bar is open seasonally with spectacular Central Park views

famousPlaces.name: The Colosseum
famousPlaces.description: The Flavian Amphitheatre — the world's largest ancient amphitheatre — was completed in 80 AD and could seat 80,000 spectators watching gladiatorial combat. Its engineering brilliance and dramatic ruins remain one of humanity's most awe-inspiring architectural achievements.
tips: Pre-book timed entry tickets online to avoid 2-hour queues
The SUPER ticket includes Roman Forum and underground arena access
Visit on a Monday when Roman Forum is less busy

famousPlaces.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
famousPlaces.description: The Vatican Museums contain one of the world's greatest art collections, accumulated over 500 years by the popes. The journey culminates in Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel — one of humanity's supreme artistic achievements, where the Creation of Adam fresco has moved visitors to tears for five centuries.
tips: Book the early morning 7AM access tour for a near-empty Sistine Chapel
Modest dress is required — cover shoulders and knees
The Gallery of Maps is often overlooked but stunningly beautiful

famousPlaces.name: Tanah Lot Temple
famousPlaces.description: One of Bali's most iconic sea temples, perched dramatically on an offshore rock formation surrounded by crashing waves. During low tide, visitors can walk across to the temple; at high tide, it becomes an island. The sunset views here are legendary among photographers and romantic travelers.
tips: Check tide times in advance — low tide gives access to the temple base
Arrive 90 minutes before sunset to secure a good viewing spot
The surrounding cliffside restaurants offer perfect sunset views with cocktails

famousPlaces.name: Tegalalang Rice Terraces
famousPlaces.description: The UNESCO-listed rice terraces of Tegalalang in Ubud are a masterpiece of traditional Balinese Subak irrigation — a 1,000-year-old cooperative water management system. The emerald green stepped paddies descend into a lush valley, offering some of Bali's most photographed landscapes.
tips: Go early to avoid tour buses and capture the morning mist
The swing above the terraces is touristy but offers incredible photo opportunities
Several cafes on the ridge offer breakfast with panoramic views

famousPlaces.name: Hagia Sophia
famousPlaces.description: Built in 537 AD as a cathedral, converted to a mosque in 1453, a museum for 85 years, and reconverted to an active mosque in 2020, Hagia Sophia is a building that embodies civilizational history. Its soaring 56-meter dome was the world's largest for nearly a millennium.
famousPlaces.openingHours: Open daily except during prayer times
tips: Entry is now free but bring appropriate attire — modest dress required
Women must cover their hair with a scarf inside
Visit just after prayer time ends for the best access to the interior

famousPlaces.name: Grand Bazaar
famousPlaces.description: One of the world's oldest and largest covered markets, the Grand Bazaar has over 4,000 shops spread across 61 covered streets and has been trading since 1461. Explore its labyrinthine alleys for hand-painted ceramics, Turkish carpets, gold jewellery, spices, and traditional lanterns.
tips: Bargaining is expected — start at 50% of the asking price
The Spice Bazaar nearby offers Turkish delight, teas, and dried fruits
Watch for tourist-trap prices near main entrances — venture deeper for better deals

famousPlaces.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
famousPlaces.description: The grandest of Seoul's five royal palaces, Gyeongbokgung was the main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty for over 500 years. Its magnificent throne hall, reflecting pond, and traditional Gyeonghoeru Pavilion stand beautifully amid the modern city skyline — a profound contrast of Korea's past and present.
famousPlaces.bestTimeToVisit: Changing of the Guard ceremony at 10AM or 2PM
tips: Rent a hanbok (traditional dress) for free entry and beautiful photos
The National Folk Museum inside the palace grounds is free and fascinating
The Changing of the Royal Guard ceremony is spectacular and free to watch

famousPlaces.name: The Grand Palace
famousPlaces.description: The official residence of the Kings of Siam since 1782, the Grand Palace is Thailand's most spectacular architectural complex — a dazzling ensemble of gilded spires, mirrored mosaic, and ornate Thai craftsmanship covering 218,000 square meters. Within its walls sits Wat Phra Kaew, home to the revered Emerald Buddha.
tips: Dress modestly — cover shoulders and knees; free clothing loans available at entry
Go early to avoid the heat and tour groups
Combine with Wat Pho temple (5 min walk) on the same visit

famousPlaces.name: Baa Atoll Biosphere Reserve
famousPlaces.description: A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and one of the world's greatest marine ecosystems, Baa Atoll is home to Hanifaru Bay — where the world's largest gatherings of manta rays and whale sharks occur seasonally. The kaleidoscopic coral reefs teem with sea turtles, eagle rays, and over 1,200 species of fish.
tips: Only snorkelling (not scuba) is permitted in Hanifaru Bay to protect the ecosystem
Book manta/whale shark excursions through your resort in advance
Calm days (no wind) are best for visibility — check conditions the night before

famousPlaces.name: Sydney Opera House
famousPlaces.description: Jørn Utzon's 1973 masterpiece is the defining symbol of Australia — its dramatic sail-shaped shell roofs housing multiple performance venues on the edge of Bennelong Point. Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007, it hosts over 1,800 performances annually and can be toured even without attending a show.
famousPlaces.bestTimeToVisit: Morning or for an evening performance
tips: Attending an evening performance offers the best interior experience
The forecourt often has free outdoor performances and events
The Opera Bar below has some of the city's best harbour sunset views

famousPlaces.name: Table Mountain
famousPlaces.description: One of the world's most recognizable natural landmarks, Table Mountain's flat-topped summit at 1,086 meters offers 360-degree views across Cape Town, the Cape Peninsula, Robben Island, and Table Bay. The aerial cableway rotates during the 5-minute ascent for panoramic views in all directions.
tips: Check the official Table Mountain website for real-time cable car status
Book cableway tickets online to avoid queues
The hike up Platteklip Gorge takes about 90 minutes and is well signposted

famousPlaces.name: Christ the Redeemer
famousPlaces.description: Perched atop the 700-meter Corcovado Mountain, the 38-meter Art Deco statue of Christ the Redeemer has watched over Rio since 1931 with arms spread wide. One of the New Seven Wonders of the World, it offers a spiritual and panoramic experience that encapsulates the beauty and soul of Rio de Janeiro.
tips: Go early on clear days — clouds frequently obscure the statue by mid-morning
Take the rack railway from Cosme Velho for the most scenic ascent
The sunset viewing experience is particularly dramatic on clear evenings

famousPlaces.name: Oia Village Sunset
famousPlaces.description: Oia's sunset is considered one of the finest in the world — crowds gather every evening on the village's medieval castle ruins to applaud as the sun melts into the Aegean Sea, silhouetting blue-domed churches against a sky of molten orange and crimson. The views across the caldera are nothing short of magical.
famousPlaces.bestTimeToVisit: 90 minutes before sunset for a good position
tips: Arrive 90 minutes early to claim a spot on the castle walls
Alternatively, watch from a caldera-view restaurant with a glass of Assyrtiko wine
The crowd applause at the moment of sunset is a uniquely moving experience

famousPlaces.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square
famousPlaces.description: The beating heart of Marrakech's medina, this UNESCO-listed square transforms dramatically at dusk — snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and henna artists give way to dozens of open-air food stalls filling the air with aromatic smoke. It's one of Earth's greatest public spectacles, unchanged in spirit for centuries.
tips: Try the fresh-squeezed orange juice from the stalls — incredibly cheap and delicious
Watch from a rooftop restaurant initially for a bird's-eye orientation
Agree on prices before accepting any entertainment or having photos taken
